result:
I fixed all 8 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match the docstrings. I wrote a reference implementation from the docstrings and the module-level rules and compared it with all 80 rules over many qty/unit combinations. Before the fix 8 rules didn't match; after it, none do.

**Fixed rules:**

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 04 | Discount was rounded with `round()` instead of cut down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 11 | The cap was applied to the amount before the percentage, not to the discount | Calculate the discount first, then `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 20 | `qty > 5`, so exactly 5 units got no discount | `qty >= 5` |
| 27 | `qty > 20`, so exactly 20 units got no discount | `qty >= 20` |
| 43 | Discount was rounded with `round()` | Changed to `// 100` |
| 47 | A "whole" rule was computed like a "marginal" one, discounting only the units above 12 | `base * 10 // 100` |
| 53 | The cap was applied to the price (`min(base, 30000)`) instead of the discount | Calculate the discount first, then `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 64 | The cap was applied to the price (`min(base, 10000)`) instead of the discount | Calculate the discount first, then `min(disc, 10000)` |

**Also changed (prices unchanged):** rules 42 and 79 used `>` where the docstring says `N+`. They only discount units above the threshold, so at exactly the threshold the discount is 0 either way. I changed them to `>=` anyway so the code matches the docstrings.

A copy of the original file is in the scratchpad as `pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
